subject: Science
title: Cellular Organization
learningOutcomes: Define a cell and identify the main parts of animal and plant cells under a microscope.
Compare animal and plant cells, listing the parts they share and the parts found only in plant cells.
Explain how specialized cells are adapted in shape and structure to carry out particular jobs.
Describe the biological hierarchy: how cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and organ systems form an organism.
Give examples of specialized cells, tissues and organs in both animals and plants.

sections.heading: Cells
sections.body: Cells are the basic building blocks of all living things — from the smallest bacteria to the largest animal. Organisms made of a single cell, such as bacteria, are unicellular, while organisms made of millions of cells joined together, like most animals and plants, are multicellular. Cells are microscopic, meaning they are so tiny they can only be seen using a microscope. Even though animal and plant cells look different inside, they carry out the same basic jobs: taking in food, releasing energy, getting rid of waste, growing and reproducing.

sections.heading: Parts of the Cell
sections.body: The nucleus is the control centre of the cell; it holds the genetic information that controls everything the cell does. The cytoplasm is a jelly-like fluid where the cell's chemical reactions take place. The cell membrane is a thin skin that controls what enters and leaves the cell. The mitochondria release energy through cellular respiration, which is why they are called the powerhouse of the cell. These four parts are found in both animal and plant cells.

sections.heading: Animal Cells vs Plant Cells
sections.body: Animal and plant cells share the nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane and mitochondria, but plant cells have three extra parts. A cell wall made of cellulose sits outside the membrane and gives the plant cell its shape and strength. Chloroplasts contain the green chemical chlorophyll and make food by photosynthesis using the Sun's energy. Plant cells also have one large central vacuole filled with cell sap, while animal cells have many small vacuoles instead. Animal cells have none of the plant-only parts because animals get their energy from the food they eat.

sections.heading: Respiration and Photosynthesis
sections.body: Two important processes happen inside cells. Cellular respiration takes place in the mitochondria: glucose is broken down to release energy that the cell uses for all its activities. Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts of plant cells: chlorophyll traps sunlight so the plant can make its own food (glucose) and release oxygen. Animal cells cannot photosynthesise because they have no chloroplasts.

sections.heading: Special Cells for Special Jobs
sections.body: In multicellular organisms, cells are specialized — each is adapted in shape and structure to do a particular job. Nerve cells have long thin fibres to carry messages around the body. Red blood cells have a large surface area to carry lots of oxygen. Muscle cells are long and thin with pointed ends so they can slide over each other to contract and relax. Epithelial cells are thin and flat, forming protective layers that line surfaces such as the skin and the alimentary canal. In plants, pollen grains are adapted for pollination — some have spiky surfaces to stick to insects, others have tiny wings to be carried by the wind.

sections.heading: Cells, Tissues, Organs and Organisms
sections.body: Living bodies are organised in a hierarchy from smallest to largest: cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism. A tissue is a group of similar cells doing the same job, such as muscle tissue. Different tissues combine to form an organ — the stomach, for example, is made of muscle, nerve and blood tissues. Organs working together form an organ system, such as the digestive, circulatory or nervous system, and all the organ systems together make up an organism. Plants show the same hierarchy: palisade cells form palisade tissue, which helps make up a leaf (an organ), which is part of the shoot system of the whole plant.

definitions.definition: The basic unit and building block of all living things.
The control centre of the cell; it contains genetic information and controls all cell activities.
The parts of the cell where energy is released by respiration; the powerhouse of the cell.
A part found only in plant cells that contains chlorophyll and makes food by photosynthesis.
A firm outer coating made of cellulose, found only in plant cells, that keeps the cell's shape.
A group of similar cells all doing the same job.
A body part made of different tissues working together, such as the stomach.
A complete living thing that can survive on its own.

examTips: The four parts shared by both animal and plant cells are the nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane and mitochondria — the three plant-only parts are the cell wall, chloroplast and large central vacuole.
Don't mix up respiration and photosynthesis: respiration happens in the mitochondria (in all cells) and releases energy; photosynthesis happens in the chloroplasts (plant cells only) and makes food.
Learn the hierarchy in order — cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism — it is one of the most commonly tested ideas in this chapter.

interactiveLesson.instructions: Explore each labelled part of the plant cell. Select every hotspot to continue.

hotspots.label: Nucleus
hotspots.fact: The nucleus is the control centre; it holds the genetic information that controls everything the cell does.

hotspots.label: Cytoplasm
hotspots.fact: The cytoplasm is a jelly-like fluid where the cell's chemical reactions take place.

hotspots.label: Cell Membrane
hotspots.fact: The cell membrane is a thin skin that controls which substances enter and leave the cell.

hotspots.label: Cell Wall
hotspots.fact: The cell wall is a firm coating of cellulose, found only in plant cells, that keeps the cell's shape.

hotspots.label: Chloroplast
hotspots.fact: Chloroplasts contain green chlorophyll and make the plant's food by photosynthesis.

hotspots.label: Large Vacuole
hotspots.fact: Plant cells have one large central vacuole filled with cell sap; animal cells have many small ones.

practiceQuestions.prompt: What are the basic building blocks of all living things?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Cells are the basic building blocks of all living things.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which of these is a unicellular organism?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Bacteria are made of a single cell, so they are unicellular.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Cells can only be seen using a microscope.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Cells are microscopic — too tiny to see with the naked eye.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which part of the cell is the control centre?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The nucleus is the control centre and holds the genetic information.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The ____ is a jelly-like fluid where chemical reactions take place.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Chemical reactions of the cell happen in the cytoplasm.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Why are mitochondria called the powerhouse of the cell?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Mitochondria release energy by breaking down glucose in cellular respiration.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Only plant cells have a cell wall.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The cell wall, made of cellulose, is found only in plant cells.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Where does photosynthesis take place in a plant cell?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Photosynthesis happens in the chloroplasts, using chlorophyll.

practiceQuestions.prompt: The green chemical in chloroplasts is called ____.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Chlorophyll traps sunlight so the plant can make food.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Why do red blood cells have a large surface area?
practiceQuestions.explanation: A large surface area lets red blood cells pick up lots of oxygen.

practiceQuestions.prompt: How is a nerve cell adapted for its job?

options: It has long thin fibres to carry messages

practiceQuestions.explanation: Nerve cells have long thin fibres that carry messages around the body.

practiceQuestions.prompt: A tissue is a group of similar cells doing the same job.
practiceQuestions.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells all doing the same job.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which tissues combine to make up the stomach?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The stomach is an organ made of muscle, nerve and blood tissues.

practiceQuestions.prompt: Which organ system carries blood around the body?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The circulatory system carries blood around the body.

practiceQuestions.prompt: All the organ systems together make up an ____.
practiceQuestions.explanation: All the organ systems together make up an organism.

sequencingActivity.prompt: Arrange the levels of organization in the correct order, from smallest to largest.
sequencingActivity.explanation: Cells group to form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and all the organ systems together make up the organism.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A scientist looks at an unknown cell under a microscope and sees a cell wall, chloroplasts and one large central vacuole. What can she correctly conclude?

options: It cannot be a living cell

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: A cell wall, chloroplasts and one large central vacuole are all plant-only parts, so it must be a plant cell.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: A cell has no chloroplasts but has many mitochondria. What does this tell you about how it gets its energy?

options: It makes its own food by photosynthesis
It cannot use energy at all
It gets energy by respiration, using food taken in from elsewhere
It only stores energy and never uses it

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: Without chloroplasts the cell cannot photosynthesise, so it must take in food and release energy through respiration in its mitochondria — like an animal cell.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: Root hair cells have a long, thin extension. Why is this shape an advantage?

options: It helps the cell carry oxygen
It increases the surface for absorbing water and minerals from the soil
It lets the cell make food
It helps the cell contract and relax

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: The long root hair gives greater reach and surface area, so the cell can absorb more water and minerals from the soil.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: Muscle tissue and nerve tissue are found working together in the stomach. What does this best show?

options: The stomach is a single cell
Different tissues combine to form an organ
Tissues and organs are the same thing
The stomach is an organ system

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: An organ such as the stomach is formed when different tissues (muscle, nerve, blood) combine and work together.

bossBattleQuestions.prompt: Caulerpa is a seaweed up to 1 metre long, yet it is described as a single cell. Why is this surprising?

options: Because most organisms that large are multicellular, made of millions of cells
Because it means Caulerpa is not alive
Because single cells are always the largest organisms

bossBattleQuestions.explanation: Organisms that large are almost always multicellular, so a single-celled organism up to a metre long is remarkable.
